newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen moving sideways before auction.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen moving sideways before auction.

text.p: Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures are expected to remain in a narrow range on Tuesday until the results of a 10-year JGB auction are announced, traders said.
"We could see more activity after auction results are announced. But until then, June is likely to hover at around 126.90," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.
The Ministry of Finance (MOF) will announce the offering at 8.30 a.m. (2330 GMT). The auction is expected to close at noon (0300 GMT) and the results to be announced at 2.30 p.m. (0530 GMT).
The coupon of the new 10-year JGB is likely to be set at 2.3 or 2.4 percent, down from 2.5 percent in the previous auction, traders said.

"The new 10-year JGB is likely to attract regional investors. So the auction is expected to produce decent results. However, life insurers might not be that keen to buy JGBs with coupon below 2.5 percent," said the trader.
If the auction goes well, JGB futures could rise before the close, possibly testing the record high of 127.34 set on April 8, traders said.
Traders said remarks by the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) regional branch managers on Monday afternoon did not provide clues about JGB directions.

Eichiro Kinoshita, executive director and general manager of the BOJ's Osaka branch office said on Monday that overall business sentiment was improving in western Japan, but gaps in sentiment among industries were widening.
The BOJ's two-day branch managers' meeting began on Monday. Traders said the market would be focusing on a news conference by BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita on Wednesday.
